what: Cross-session reproducibility check on the grouped kernel, and what it invalidates
same_code: The v4 kernel measured in this run is byte-identical in the hot path to v3: same int32 word loads, same scale broadcast, same accumulate. Only the sweep grid was widened (bn 1-16, bw 8-96, warps 1-8).
conclusion: This is a reproducibility failure at the 22% level across sessions on identical code. It is larger than most of the optimisations measured today, which means the series 46.8 -> 59.3 -> 68.8 cannot be treated as a clean progression: the last step may be partly environment.
what_is_affected: 68.8 GB/s is withdrawn as a stable figure and stands as one sample, the highest of two taken on the same code.
The v2 result (59.3) was measured in a session where v3's first run also landed at 59.0 on default settings, so 59.3 agrees with itself and is the more credible number.
The v3 gain of 16% over v2 is inside the 22% cross-session band and is therefore NOT established. It may be real or may be a favourable session.
what_survives: The grouped-expert change: 27.8 -> 46.8, reproduced twice at 46.2 and 46.8 in different sessions, a 1.3% agreement.
The scale broadcast: 46.8 -> 51.6 on default and 59.3 on sweep, measured in one session that also re-measured its own default at 59.0, so it is internally consistent.
The duration finding: 16.7 GB/s at a 1.4 ms run against 38.0 at 20 ms, which was measured inside a single run and is a within-run comparison.

what_the_number_should_be_quoted_as.safe_range: 54-69 GB/s on the best tile, with 59 as the best-supported single figure
what_the_number_should_be_quoted_as.position: at best 89% of parity, at worst 70%, and not yet sufficient to beat the baseline end to end

process_fix: Every future kernel claim must be the median of at least 3 runs in at least 2 separate Kaggle sessions, and reported with the spread. A single session's best figure is a sample, not a result. This pass exists because I did not apply that rule to v3.
